COLDWAR_colonial_affairs_category_desc: The Cabinet Secretariat maintains the government's papers on overseas administration, internal security and confidential foreign liaison. Ministers may review territorial settlements, consider reports on domestic organisations and authorise assistance abroad. Standing appropriations are charged to the weekly national budget.
COLDWAR_COL_tab_territory_tt:
§YThe Overseas Secretariat§!
Territorial dossiers place local resistance, cooperation, economic restrictions and weekly appropriations before cabinet. Papers are opened only for an active overseas administration under this government's authority. These domestic records require no foreign intelligence network.

§YThe administrative settlement§!
Ministers may retain Civil Administration, fund Development and Representation, impose Security Administration or pursue Negotiated Self-Government. A new mandate remains in force for §Y180 days§!. Self-government is an administrative course; independence requires a further political settlement.

§YPetitions and expenditure§!
Territorial representatives may request a grant or consultation. §YRespond§! brings a pending petition before cabinet; each response states its payment and local consequences. Standing appropriations enter the weekly national budget.
COLDWAR_COL_tab_internal_tt:
§YThe internal security cabinet§!
Domestic dossiers assess an organisation's strength, outside assistance and the demands placed on the security services. They belong to the government responsible for the case and require no foreign intelligence network.

§YNorthern Ireland / IRA§!
An active British case brings organisation strength, community tension and policing appropriations before ministers. Policing mandates and §YMeasures§! cover investigations, reform, emergency detention, confidential ceasefire contacts and constitutional talks, subject to their stated conditions.

§YFederal Republic of Germany / RAF§!
From §Y14 May 1970§!, an active RAF case reports cadres, milieu, generation and foreign assistance. The federal security cabinet handles investigations, wanted persons, protection and prison policy. Additional programmes depend on the relevant institutional authority and national policy.

Where no active case falls within this government's jurisdiction, the Secretariat supplies a briefing in place of an organisation dossier.
COLDWAR_COL_tab_contacts_tt:
§YConfidential foreign liaison§!
The intelligence service may approach colonial movements, organisations in occupied territories and active IRA or RAF contacts. A dossier can be placed before ministers only where an organisation is active and reliable regional sources exist. Establishing a network does not itself create a movement.

§YAuthority to open a dossier§!
An intelligence agency and a regional network §Ystrictly above 50% in the state concerned§! are required. Operatives must establish sources in that area; coverage in a neighbouring state is insufficient. Territories controlled by this government, its subjects or its overlord fall outside foreign liaison.

§YThe regional papers§!
§YNext authorised contact§! brings the next accessible dossier before cabinet. It remains unavailable while no contact qualifies. A qualifying state also offers §YRegional file§! in its map panel. Papers identify the movement and assess its strength and assistance; RAF reports distinguish cadres from milieu.

§YMinisterial commitments§!
Cabinet may authorise political backing, financial assistance or equipment shipments. The §YSupport§! papers state the price, effect, term, limits and risk of public disclosure. Loss of regional access suspends further commitments and withdraws the dossier. Assistance already delivered runs its remaining term while the recipient remains eligible.
